items.title: UK Hindu family takes legal action after school objects to boy wearing tilak
points: The parents of a nine-year-old British Hindu boy, who was withdrawn from his primary school in London after it objected to him wearing a tilak on his forehead, have initiated legal proceedings in the UK High Court.

The boy, who belongs to the Swaminarayan faith tradition, had attended Vicar’s Green Primary School in west London since 2021 and worn his religious marking, known as the Tilak-Chandlo, without difficulty.
However, the school objected to the practice in late 2025, triggering a dispute that eventually led his parents to withdraw him from the school and pursue legal action.
“He had worn his Tilak-Chandlo to school for years without difficulty, and we never imagined that something so sacred to our family would become a source of distress,” they said.
The family is represented by Ashray Law, which has filed proceedings alleging religious discrimination under the UK’s Equality Act 2010 and breaches of rights protected by the Human Rights Act 1998.

items.title: [OPINION] NoPixel V Shows Us What GTA 6 UGC Could Look Like
points: For years, GTA 5 has been one of the clearest examples of how far a game can stretch beyond what its developer originally built.
Rockstar created Los Santos as a huge playground, then gave players years to find new ways to use it through GTA Online, mods, and roleplay.
However, watching NoPixel V footage made me realise just how much further that idea can go in terms of GTA 6 UGC when creators are given the tools to reshape the world itself.

Some of these experiences have also reached enormous audiences, with Blox Fruits surpassing 64 billion visits and games like Grow a Garden and Steal a Brainrot reaching more than 20 million concurrent players during their peaks.
Even with Rockstar introducing the in-depth Rockstar Mission Creator for branching custom missions in late 2025, true world-building on the scale of a custom server stayed locked behind PC modding.
These creator communities then expanded the possibilities of GTA 5 Online.

items.title: Karnataka Minister Challenges Oil Companies: Will Provide Proof Of Excess Ethanol In Petrol On Monday
points: Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad has issued a fresh warning to oil marketing companies after they rejected the state government's allegations of excessive ethanol blending in petrol.
The minister has said that he will release a detailed response to their clarification on Monday, promising to put the Karnataka government's position before the entire nation.
The state had earlier shared test results that reportedly showed ethanol concentrations of up to 31.2% in an Indian Oil petrol sample.
Another sample collected from a Hindustan Petroleum outlet was reported to contain 30.5% ethanol.
The government had said that it collected 63 samples from seven districts, including Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru.
They maintained that petrol supplied across India, including Karnataka, complies with IS 17021, the relevant Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline.

items.title: "This Is Not a Political Book": Sonia Gandhi Explains Why She Wrote Her Memoir

"For most of my life, I kept my inner world to myself.

items.title: Rajnath Singh Celebrates Diwali With Army At Indo-China Border In Sikkim
points: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh celebrated Diwali with Indian Army personnel at the Sherathang War Memorial near Nathula in Sikkim, along the India-China border, on Sunday, paying tribute to soldiers who laid down their lives in the service of the nation.
The Defence Minister arrived at Sherathang by helicopter from the Sukna Army Base in West Bengal, accompanied by Chief of Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth and other senior Army officials.

Addressing the troops, Singh said the country's ability to celebrate Diwali peacefully was made possible by the sacrifices and dedication of its armed forces.
